Offing compared with endoflife.date

endoflife.date is a community database of end-of-life dates with a public API. Offing bundles reviewed lifecycle rules and checks a repository against them. The two answer different halves of the same question.

What endoflife.date does better

  • Breadth. The product directory covers products across many vendors, maintained by contributors rather than one project's rule set.
  • A hosted API. Consumers can query dates over HTTP instead of shipping data with a tool; the API documentation describes the endpoints and response shape.
  • Upstream by design. A product page is the canonical place to check a date without installing anything (example: Node.js).

What Offing adds

  • Repository context. Offing maps a lifecycle rule to the file, line, and usage in the repository, so the answer includes what is affected (ARCHITECTURE.md).
  • Offline operation. Scans use bundled or cached, verified data and never make a request (DATA.md); CI does not depend on a third-party endpoint.
  • Review dates in the result. Every scan says which data version it used and how old the evidence is, and warns when it is stale (DATA.md).
  • Migration context. Findings carry replacements and verification steps for the change (MIGRATION_PACKETS.md).

Use them together

  1. Check the upstream date and its source on endoflife.date.
  2. Run offing scan . to see whether the repository uses the affected release and where.
  3. When the repository needs a pinned data version for reproducible CI, follow DATA.md instead of relying on a live API response.
